title: Deceptive Patterns Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of deceptive design patterns

questions.question: Which one of these deceptive patterns involves making a service easy to sign up for but difficult to opt out off?
questions.explanation: Roach Motel is the patterns where the process of cancelling a service is more difficult compared to signing in.

questions.question: Which one of these options describes the Fake Scarcity patterns?
options: Trick users in impulse purchases by limiting the availability of a product
Guilt-Tripping users in agreeing to something they would not do in normal circumstances
Users are charged automatically without warning after using a free trial
The proper pricing information is obstracted, making price comparison more difficult
questions.explanation: In Fake Scarcity, the user is tricked into thinking there is a limited stock of an item, making them more likely to make an impulsive purchase.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves the process of adding additional items in a user’s basket without their consent?
questions.explanation: Default Opt-In is the pattern where an item is added to a users' basket without their knowledge in hopes of not noticing it before the checkout process is finished.

questions.question: Which one of these options describe the Hidden Cost pattern?
options: An item is displayed at a fake discount, and the “Real” price is artificially inflated
The correct pricing information is obscured
Users are charged for a service without warning right after a free trial expires
Unexpected costs are initially hidden before the checkout process
questions.explanation: Hidden Cost is the pattern where additional fees are initially hidden from the user, only to be added during the checkout process.

questions.question: Which one of these options describes the Disguised Ads pattern?
options: Sites are poorly designed in hope of making crucial information harder to be read by the user
Prompts and pop-ups are constantly displayed to the user
Ads are designed to blend in a site’s interface, in hope of tricking the user into clicking and engaging with them
questions.explanation: Disguised Ads involves the process to make the adds blend into the site’s layout, increasing the chances of users interacting with them.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves the process of displaying a fake discount, with an inflated price as a before price?
questions.explanation: This pattern involves in tricking the user into thinking a sale for a specific price happens by displaying a fake discount price and a fake before price.

questions.question: Which one of these options involves the process of guilt tripping the user into agreeing to something they wouldn't do in normal circumstances?
questions.explanation: Confirm Shaming is the patterns where a user is forced to agree by using manipulative wording that makes them think bad for saying no.

questions.question: Which one of these options describe the Bundled Consent pattern?
options: Users find cancelling a service harder or mor tedious than signing up for it
Items are added to a user’s basket without their knowledge
Users are forced to agree to something extra
Additional costs are hidden before the checkout process
questions.explanation: Bundled Consent is the pattern where a user is forced to agree to something extra if they wish to complete an action.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves constantly showing pop-ups or prompts to pressure the user into making a decision?
questions.explanation: Nagging is the pattern where users are repeatedly interrupted with prompts or pop-ups, pressuring them into taking an action they might not otherwise choose.

questions.question: Which one of these options describes the Free Trial Trap pattern?
options: Users are tricked into buying items through fake discounts
Users are automatically charged after a free trial ends without clear warning
Users are forced to agree to additional terms
Pricing information is hidden during checkout
questions.explanation: Free Trial Trap occurs when users sign up for a free trial but are automatically charged once it ends, often without clear reminders.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves making it difficult for users to compare prices between products?
questions.explanation: This pattern obscures or complicates pricing information, making it harder for users to compare options and make informed decisions.

questions.question: Which one of these options describes the Interface Interference pattern?
options: Users are tricked into impulse purchases with fake urgency
The design of the interface is manipulated to mislead users or hide information
Items are added to a basket without consent
Users are charged after a free trial
questions.explanation: Interface Interference uses design tricks like poor contrast or misleading layouts to confuse users or hide important details.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves forcing users to accept additional conditions to proceed?
questions.explanation: Bundled Consent forces users to agree to extra, often unrelated conditions if they want to complete an action.

questions.question: Which one of these options describes the Default Opt-In pattern?
options: Users are tricked into thinking items are limited
Items or services are automatically selected or added without user consent
questions.explanation: Default Opt-In occurs when options are pre-selected or items are added without the user’s knowledge, relying on them not noticing.

questions.question: Which one of these patterns involves manipulating users by making them feel like they will miss out?
questions.explanation: Fake Scarcity creates a false sense of urgency by suggesting limited availability, pushing users to act quickly out of fear of missing out.
